citations.quote: the message does not logically exist for the MCS and hence shall not be sent to a destination
An implementation may optionally provide the elements specified in Annex A, Communications facility.

cases.reason: No 2023 counterpart: the pointer GR-14.9.38.4-x is the 2023 asynchronous-messaging SEND (a run unit sends to a message server), a different facility; its witnesses (MessagingProcessTests, send-no-server, send-group-holding-tag) are refused at --std 2002 (COBOL0878, E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/op-20261114/read-2002/out/probes-u-45/ptr/send-no-server-2002.out) and show nothing about the MCS. The 2002 rule is Annex A (optional per §2002:3.1). The compiler provides the facility at --std 2002 (COBOL0903 obsolete warning only). The code and test pointer is the 1985 twin 1985-GR-XIV.3.6.4-7 (CONFORMS, witness accept:[85]). Differing words from 1985: 'which'->'that', 'cannot be sent'->'shall not be sent'; nothing a program can see. The disposition is undefined, the non-delivery is testable and holds at 2002.
cases.needs: its own verdict: at --std 2002 an unterminated portion is not delivered, within the run unit or to a later run unit (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/op-20261114/read-2002/out/probes-u-45/gr7-results.txt, E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/op-20261114/read-2002/out/probes-u-45/send/1985-GR-XIV_3_6_4-8-2002.out). refute.root-cause-note: Four of the five overturns share one mechanism: at --std 2002 the compiler classifies compiler-directive words by the 2023 list (§2023:8.12, cited in its own diagnostics COBOL2650/COBOL0718/COBOL0711) instead of the 2002 list (§2002:8.12). 2002 reserves FLAG-85, FLAG-NATIVE-ARITHMETIC and 2002's exception-names; 2023 instead reserves PUSH, POP, REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH, EQUATE, UNDEFINE, FLAG-02, FLAG-14, the 2014/2023 exception-names, and more. So legal 2002 directives that use a 2023-only directive word as a compilation-variable-name or file-name are refused, and 2002-illegal ones that use FLAG-85 are accepted. The 2002 rows that defer to the list (7.2.7.3.2 SR1, 7.2.9.2 SR1, 7.2.19.2 SR1/SR2) carry it into every format that admits a defined condition or a TURN file-name.

cases.reason: The 2002 format's intrinsic-function-name-1 ranges over 2002's intrinsic functions only (2002 GR14: 'the intrinsic-function-names defined in 8.11'). The 2002 text has no FORMATTED-DATE (grep count 0), but 2023 does (§2023:15.39.1). So 'FUNCTION FORMATTED-DATE INTRINSIC' does not match the 2002 format. At --std 2002 the compiler accepts it with no diagnostic (r1_repo_intr-2002.out: ABC, exit 0). The 2023 verdict accepts the same line, so it says nothing about the 2002 exclusion. The declaration is ignored afterwards: a use of FORMATTED-DATE(...) gives COBOL1639 at 2002 (r1c), so the program fails later, not at the REPOSITORY entry. The REPOSITORY check is missing at 2023 as well: 'FUNCTION NO-SUCH-FUNC INTRINSIC' is accepted at both editions (r1e), a lead against the 2023 row FMT-12.3.8.2. The rest of the reader's scope (specifier shapes, period placement) holds.
